stories.title: Edit the data of a policy value by its kind
stories.what: Let a person change the data of a value in a policy file with the entry that fits its kind: a text box for text, a number box for numbers, a multi-line box for lists of text.
stories.why: Raw editing of a policy file is only safe when each value is edited in a form that matches what it holds, and when kinds the editor cannot handle are refused instead of damaged.

criteria.says: Given a value of a plain or expandable text kind, when the person edits it, then a text box showing its current data is offered.
Given a value of a 32-bit or 64-bit number kind, when the person edits it, then a number box showing its current data is offered.
Given a value that is a list of text, when the person edits it, then a multi-line box showing its current data is offered.
Given a value of any other kind, such as binary, when the person tries to edit it, then they see "This value kind is not supported." and nothing changes.
Given an edit dialog is open, when the person cancels it, then the value keeps its data exactly as it was.
Given the person confirms new data, when the edit is applied, then the value holds the new data, keeps its name and kind, and stays selected.

stories.title: Download the fixed Microsoft policy template package
stories.what: Fetch the one Microsoft package of administrative templates, the Windows 11 September 2026 Update (26H2), into a scratch folder on the person's computer, through the service rather than the browser.
stories.why: People who lack current policy definitions need them from Microsoft without hunting for the right download; a fixed package and secure connections keep the result predictable and safe.

criteria.says: Given the person starts the download, when it runs, then the Windows 11 September 2026 Update (26H2) administrative templates are saved as "W11Admx.msi" in a scratch folder under their local application data.
Given the person wants another version, when they start the download, then no choice of version is offered and the same package is fetched.
Given a download is made, when the connection is opened, then only TLS 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 are accepted and no other protocol is used.
Given the Microsoft site cannot be reached, when the download is started, then the failure is reported as a normal outcome and the screens never contact the site themselves.

open: Should the download still allow TLS 1.0 and 1.1, which are long retired, or only TLS 1.2 and later?

stories.title: Stamp the program with its Git version at build time
stories.what: When the program is built, work out its version from the source history and make it available to the running program, leaving the committed source with an empty version.
stories.why: Support and people reporting problems need to know exactly which build they run, without anyone typing a version by hand.

criteria.says: Given the source history has tags, when the build script runs, then the program's version is the tag, the commit count and the short commit name.
Given the source history has no tags, when the build script runs, then the program's version is the short commit name.
Given someone runs the build script or the release workflow runs it, when it finishes, then the version replaces the empty one in what the program reports.
Given the source is committed, when its version is read, then it is empty, because only a build carries a version.

stories.title: Read and write remembered preferences in the preference store
stories.what: Give the program one place to read and write named preference rows in the preference store, which carries on with defaults when it cannot be reached.
stories.why: Remembered choices must survive between runs, yet an unreachable store must never stop someone from working or interrupt them with alerts.

terms.name: Preference store
terms.means: The place where the program keeps the person's remembered choices between runs; it is not the policy files being edited.

criteria.says: Given the preference store is reachable, when a named preference is saved and read back, then the saved value is returned.
Given the preference store cannot be opened or created, when preferences are read, then they read as their defaults.
Given the preference store cannot be opened or created, when the person changes a preference, then the change is dropped and nothing is remembered at the next run.
Given the preference store cannot be reached, when the program carries on, then the person is not told.

open: Existing settings in the old Windows registry location are not carried over; should a one-time import of them be planned?

stories.title: Keep the person's remembered choices for the rest of the program
stories.what: Give the rest of the program typed access to the remembered choices: the chosen sources, the definitions folder, the language, whether the caution was accepted and whether the offer was considered.
stories.why: Every part of the program that needs a remembered choice gets it the same way, so choices are kept and returned consistently.

terms.name: Remembered choice
terms.means: A decision the person made that the program keeps between runs, such as language or definitions folder; it is not a policy setting.

criteria.says: Given a chosen source, definitions folder, language, caution acceptance or offer consideration is saved, when it is asked for later, then the same choice is returned.
Given a choice was never saved, when it is asked for, then its default is returned.
Given the preference store cannot be reached, when a choice is saved or asked for, then the program carries on with defaults and tells no one.
